summary.text: Daughter of Oceanus who bore to the river Inachus the first Argive line: Phoroneus, whom the Argives call their first man, and Aegialeus, after whom Aegialia was named.

story.text: Apollodorus gives her one sentence and a dynasty: of Inachus and Melia, daughter of Ocean, were born sons, Phoroneus and Aegialeus — a bare parentage formula, with no word of marriage. Aegialeus died childless, leaving the country the name Aegialia; through Phoroneus, who reigned over all the land later called the Peloponnese, she is grandmother of Apis and of Niobe, the first mortal woman with whom Zeus lay.

Hyginus strikes her from the record: in his telling Inachus begets Phoroneus by his own sister Argia, an Oceanid of his preface's catalogue, and Melia appears nowhere in the Argive line at all. The mother of the first man of Argos is one nymph in Apollodorus and another in Hyginus — and in the local traditions Pausanias gathered at Argos, no mother is named for Phoroneus whatsoever.
